title: Owl Post — Tidekeeper Night Notes
content:
Context:
This is my mid-to-late night scratchpad for the "tidekeeper" rotation — super lightweight, meant for the person taking the 00:00-08:00 window. Not an official runbook yet; it contains temporary workarounds, quick commands, and a few reminders I keep forgetting.

Quick summary (first 5 mins):
- Check PagerDuty for any active alerts tagged 'runtime' or 'cache'.
- Look at /status (internal) and the last 1 hour latency graph for redis-kv and model-proxy.
- If token queue > 120s: scale-proxy path (below).

Common triage checklist (order matters):
1) Is the alert noise or real? (look for >=2 services failing or >5% error ratio)
2) Identify namespace/service: model-proxy | kv-cache | scheduler | autoscaler.
3) Check recent deploys: slack #deploys for the last 2 hours or `git log` on infra PRs.
4) Apply quick mitigations (cache flush, revert route) and notify the on-call rotation.

Commands I use a lot (be careful with prod):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime\- shows flapping pods
- curl -sS http://model-proxy.internal/health | jq '.'
- redis-cli -h redis-cache-1 info | grep -E 'used_memory|mem_fragmentation'
- /opt/tools/scale-proxy --service model-proxy --inc 2 --reason "tidekeeper emergency"

Temporary workaround: stalled KV cache (seen 2026-02-22)
- Symptom: cache miss rate spikes to 85%, model-proxy latency jumps, token queue grows.
- Short patch: run `redis-cli -h redis-cache-1 ACL SETUSER temp-repopulate on` then trigger `cache-repopulate --pattern service:* --parallel 6` (10–15 min).
- Follow up: open JIRA-8974 and tag infra-team for a proper root cause.

Escalation matrix (fast):
- Level 1: Tidekeeper (you) — attempt mitigations, estimate 15–30m recovery.
- Level 2: Marcus Lee (eng-sre lead) — if mitigations fail or >30m outage. Slack @marcus or call.
- Level 3: Pager + Exec alert (on-call manager) if SLA impact >10% or >60m ongoing.

Known flaky things (notes-to-self):
- autoscaler sometimes double-spawns when CPU probes delayed — check HorizontalPodAutoscaler events.
- model-proxy GC spikes on longer sequences; try smaller batch-size as temporary config.
- DNS TTL bug in staging-promote script; if route flip fails, run `dig` and reapply ingress host annotation.

Recent incident TL;DR (2026-02-22 01:12):
- Cause: burst of long context requests + stale KV entries -> cascade of cache thrash.
- Fix applied: triggered cache-repopulate + bumped proxy replicas by 3.
- Postmortem action items: paged to infra team to add better eviction policy (JIRA-8974).

Notes to relievers (what I usually forget to say):
- If you see a single API path with >70% errors but infra looks green, check the rate-limiter logs for that key (it often means bad client).
- Beware of manual restarts during deploy windows (00:30–01:30) — talk on #sre-before-restart.

Minor TODOs (for next tidekeeper iteration):
- Convert this cheatpad into a real draft runbook: expand steps and add screenshots of dashboards.
- Add scripted cache-repopulate wrapper that validates success and posts status to #ops.
- Add small playbook for model-proxy A/B rollback (commands + safety checks).

Random scraps (for memory):
- A couple of helpful log grep patterns I use: `grep -E "(ERR|WARN).*kv|cache|token" -n` and `jq '.latency.p95' < metrics.json`
- If you need to simulate the load spike, use load-sim with --seq-len 1024 and --parallel 40 but warn on slack.

Last check before handing off:
- Confirm no active pages in last 10m and token queue < 30s.
- Leave a one-line status in #tidekeeper-hand-off: `ok — cache repopulated, proxy +3 replicas, monitoring green`.

Questions I still have / follow up:
- Is there an automated guard to prevent cache-repopulate during backups? (I suspect we don't)
- Can the autoscaler be taught to consider token-queue-length as a metric? File ticket if not.

If you get paged and everything is confusing: breathe, do these two things first — check PD, check /status; then ping Marcus.

-- Evelyn
